deep.reconstruction:
Page: Litt. H, folio [66] of bundle Brouillons1805, a dense page of seven-place logarithmic arithmetic with almost no prose. German labels only: Erste/Zweite/Neue/Wahre Hypothese, suppos./invent., Error, Minu, M suppos. It is a trial-and-error (hypothesis-and-correct) determination of an orbit, apparently an elliptic orbit of the 1805 comet, from three observations. This is inferred from the bundle title and from the 'elliptische Elemente' (e = sin phi = 0.7168, a 'Parabel' comparison) on the next page; I cannot confirm which body from this page alone.

(1) Left column: the end of the 'Zweite Hypothese' (the trial value 176 deg 28' 9.67'', i.e. 3 deg 31' 50'' as the supplement). Table: 0.0565039 and 0.0119027 are logs, and their differences and quarters (0.0446012 -> 0.0111503 etc.) are converted to angles (0 deg 44' 7'' ...; 0 deg 18' 48''). Angles and tabular logs (8.4095723, 8.0391488 ...) feed a series. The additive constant 0.8333333.3 (= 5/6) plus small terms (49174.9 and 14506.6 in units of 1e-7) gives 0.8382508 and 0.8347840. These look like the 5/6-based series for a sector/triangle ratio, but I am unsure of the exact formula. Then 0.0342033 / 0.0023976 are differences, 9.7026479 / 9.7001242 and 8.7634202 / 8.1357182 are log factors, and 7.00455 / 2.01919 are the resulting small quantities. The control quantity is k''/k: supposed 0.0023620, found 0.0023630, Error -10 (units 1e-7, sign = supposed minus found). Second control: 9.9744089 + (48321 + 89958 - 43144 = 95135) units gives 9.9839224 ('Minu', the found M) against 9.9836330 ('M supp.'); Error -2894. The marginal 14.52.4''32 / 8.17.35''82 are two angles obtained from this hypothesis.

(2) Middle top: a three-column side computation (49174.85/14506.65; 47888.43/13928.90; 47492.79/13748.49). Differences are formed (8644.95, 2356.80; 11214.44, 3020.36; 12026.62, 3228.23), logged (6.9367626 etc.), multiplied by log cos-type factors (9.9996244 ...), then combined with 8.2935826 etc. to give pairs 8.6428043/8.6430536, 8.7652987/8.7651871, 8.7986989/8.7987884. Their differences (+2493, -1096 or -1066, +895) are error residuals for three trial values; the same numbers (+895, -1066) reappear on the next page in the table of trial angles 3 deg 9'35'', 3 deg 15', 3 deg 24', 3 deg 31'50''. The remaining lines (9.1162659 ..., 0.0305254 ..., 9.1467913 ...) add and subtract logs for the three trials. Exact meaning of each log is unclear to me.

(3) 'Neue Hypothese': trial angle 176 deg 36' 0''. The four angle differences are 176 deg 36' minus the three longitudes-type angles 122 36 1.00, 124 1 49.02, 3 30 16.04, and plus 21 12 39.41: 53 59 59.00, 52 34 10.98, 173 5 43.96, 197 48 39.41 (all correct). Constant logs 9.0678591 and 9.3817101 (carried from the previous page) are corrected by 0.0009780 and 0.0033735 to give f = 9.0668811 and f'' = 9.3783366 (my reading: these are log values). Then log sin 53 59 59'' = 9.9079561 is subtracted from the constant 9.9191376 to give r' = 0.0111815 (the page reads 0.0111865 in the ink but the later arithmetic uses 0.0111815). f' = 9.5455516. f + f'' = 9.5509804 (check: 0.11665 + 0.23897 = 0.35562 gives log 9.5509 OK). The ratio (f+f'')/f' = 10^0.0054293 = 1.012579953 (correct). Then 8.0996790 (log of the 1/ratio-type correction, unclear), 8.1485392 (a constant), 9.9511398, and 0.0335446; sum 9.9846843 = M supposed.

A second chain (0.4786700, 0.1672145; 9.8313070, 9.7549136 ...) computes r'' = 9.9928925 and the angles 33 16 32.12, 139 52 43.96 (+ 9.5947445 etc.) and the angles 167 9 23.08, 195 27 57.04, 181 18 40.06, 14 9 16.98; sines of the angle sums lead to the angle 11 deg 34' 50'' and 23 deg 9' 40.15''. The long 'half-angle' block (3.43.1.68 / 2.4.23.955; 0.0541933 - 0.0111815 = 0.0430118, divided by 4 = 0.0107529; 0 deg 42'33'', 1.25.6.50, 0.36.11.50) turns log differences into arcs, whose log tan or log sin (8.3937869, 8.0223507, 8.8117614, 8.5584491) enter the same series as before: 0.8333333.3 + 48565.72 (units 1e-7) = 0.8381899, 0.8333333 + 14234.47 = 0.8347567.5. Results: k''/k supposed 23955, found 23954, Error +1 (units 1e-7). The 'M' line: 9.9752772 + (48042 + 89320 - 43514 = 93848) = 9.9846620 ('Minu'); compared with M supposed 9.9846843 the difference is -223 in 1e-7 units (supposed minus found = +223). The page seems to read -1223 (possibly a slip or a misread). The lower-right block repeats the evaluation of 48565.72 and 14234.44 with logs 6.9933705 / 6.4263593, 9.9995721 / 9.9998841, 8.2891252 / 7.7224634 for a check of the Neue values (digits partly illegible).

Purpose: the unknown is an angle (here the supplement 3 deg 24' of 176 deg 36'). For each trial value the two controls (k''/k and M) are computed twice, once 'supposed' (assumed) and once 'invented' (found); the residuals are collected (see the next page: +4436/+895, +3357/-1066, 3 deg 31'50'' -2894/+1493) and the 'Wahre Hypothese' 3 deg 15' 47'' (176 deg 35' 13'') is obtained by interpolation. This is a Newton/regula falsi style iteration done by hand with seven-place logs.
errors: Subtraction slip: 16976.72 - 13748.49 = 3228.23, but the page writes 3228.53 and its log 6.5090048 matches 3228.53 (log of 3228.23 would be 6.5089645). Effect about 4e-5 in the log, small.
Possible slip: 59102.87 - 47888.43 = 11214.44; the page seems to show 11214.34 (digit overwritten). Resulting log 7.0497767 lies between the two values, so unclear which was used.

Residual in the second column of the middle table: 8.7651871 - 8.7652987 = -1116 in 1e-7 units, but the page (and the next page) give -1066 (or -1096). Digits are overwritten; may be a slip or a misreading on my side.

Neue Hypothese: 9.9846620 - 9.9846843 = -223 (units 1e-7); the page writes 'Error -1223' (or +1223 / -223 crossed out on the next page). The magnitude disagrees with the arithmetic, so either a slip or a scan reading problem.

The log 8.8117614 is stated next to 3 deg 43' 1.68''; log sin of that angle is 8.8117808, a difference of about 2e-5, equivalent to an angle slip of about 0.17''. May be a small slip or an unreliable reading.

r' is written 0.0111865 in several places while 9.9191376 - 9.9079561 = 0.0111815 and the later 0.0430118 = 0.0541933 - 0.0111815 use 0.0111815; the digit looks overwritten, so probably only a reading issue.
Nothing else checked fully; many log values on the page were not independently verified.

results.what: Trial-and-error (regula falsi) solution for the angle fixing an elliptic orbit from three observations, with 'supposed' vs 'found' control quantities (k''/k and M) and interpolation of errors to a 'Wahre Hypothese'
results.modern_name: Iterative (fixed-point / secant) orbit determination from three observations; differential correction by interpolation of residuals
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria motus corporum coelestium, 1809; Ceres work 1801); Olbers for the comet method

results.what: Seven-place logarithmic evaluation of the sector/triangle-type series (5/6 + small terms) and half-angle log-to-arc conversions
results.modern_name: Series for the ratio of sector to triangle in Kepler motion (Euler-Lambert / Gauss y-series); hyperbolic-type log-to-arc conversion

results.what: Result of the iteration: true hypothesis 176 deg 35' 13'' (3 deg 15' 47'') and elliptic elements (e = sin phi = 0.7168) on the next page
results.modern_name: Orbital elements of a short-period comet orbit (elliptic) from three-observation determination

deep.surprise_reason: Routine hand computation in Gauss's own established orbit-determination style (trial hypotheses, supposed vs found controls, interpolation of the error); no new method visible. The page is only the working of one hypothesis, and what is computed is not fully recoverable without the neighbouring pages.
